marta: Quick sync — I want to nail down the partial-diversion + emergency-reversepath behavior for RB/A-B flows. TL;DR: capability to steer X% traffic to variant, but with an automatic reverse within Ns when capacity or quality drops. Thoughts?
pranav: +1. Two immediate constraints: 1) we need a single canonical signal source for quality (not multiple heuristic votes), 2) session-affinity must survive the reversal if possible.
sam: For signal source — we should prefer the telemetry service (trace + error-rate), not per-router heuristics. Router heuristics are useful for transient local failures but shouldn’t trigger global reverse.
jen: Agree on canonical signal. Also: what's the time window for rollback? seconds, minutes? We need to balance noise vs speed.
emily: I'd vote for tiered thresholds: fast reverse for high-sev errors (5xx spike), slower for quality regressions (LLM eval score drift). e.g. immediate reverse if error_rate > 5% sustained > 30s; otherwise decayed scoring over 5m.
marta: That aligns. We also need capacity-aware triggers: if variant consumes more GPU mem/calls and backend OOMs rise, trigger reversal even if error_rate low.
pranav: Right — add capacity_budget_exhausted signal from infra (queue wait > T, OOM spikes). Combine with quality: if any high-priority signal -> emergency revert.
sam: Operational detail: reversal should support three modes — cold-cut (instant all traffic back), staged-backoff (reduce weight by factor), and throttle-redirect (send excess to dedicated fallback pool). Which do we implement first?
jen: Implement staged-backoff first. Cold-cut is scary for client-side affinity; staged gives smoother transitions and better observability.
emily: Also: preserve KV/prefix caches. If we flip too fast we kill KV warmups and increase latency. Consider a reverse path that marks requests as "replay-friendly" for a TTL to allow cache reconciliation.
marta: Good call. Let's capture config prototype.
pranav: Draft policy snippet: ```json
{
  "variant_policy": {
    "target_fraction": 0.2,
    "staged_steps": [0.2,0.1,0.0],
    "emergency_signals": {
      "error_rate": {"threshold":0.05, "window_s":30, "priority":"high"},
      "oom_rate": {"threshold":0.01, "window_s":60, "priority":"high"},
      "eval_score_drop": {"threshold":0.02, "window_s":300, "priority":"medium"}
    },
    "affinity_ttl_s":300
  }
}
```
sam: That seems reasonable. Need to add a field for capacity_penalty_weight and a latency_p95_guardrail. Also a max_retries_for_rollforward to avoid oscillation.
jen: +1 on oscillation guard; add cool-down period after any reversal. E.g. cool_down_s = 600.
emily: For observability: add a dedicated dashboard with a single rollcall metric 'variant_state' (states: ramping, steady, degrading, reverted) and a single audit log event for any automatic reversal with all signals attached.
argo-bot: deploy-check: staleness note — make sure any policy config change includes a schema bump. Detected potential collision with existing rollout-controller v2 schema.
marta: Good point. We'll target rollout-controller v3 for this. Action items: 1) prana — add capacity signals and oscillation params to policy; 2) sam — implement staged-backoff in controller runtime; 3) jen — UX for cool-down/override in console; 4) emily — telemetry dashboard template + eval hook. I'll open a tracking issue.
pranav: I'll sketch capacity signal shapes and submit PR for policy schema.
sam: I'll prototype staged-backoff algorithm and run sim locally (load generator).
jen: I'll mock console settings for emergency revert and manual cutover.
emily: Will prepare dashboard & an alert runbook for SRE on auto-revert.
marta: Thanks — short follow-up meeting tomorrow 10:00. If anyone sees immediate blockers call it out here. :thumbsup:
